title: Consciousness exists in an inclusive sense, mischaracterized as phenomenal

statements.text: Illusionism denies phenomenal consciousness properly so called, not consciousness. There is a form of consciousness that consists in having states with quasi-phenomenal properties and is commonly mischaracterized as phenomenal. In the inclusive sense of states that might turn out to be phenomenal or only quasi-phenomenal, realists and illusionists agree that consciousness exists.

sources.quote: In this sense realists and illusionists agree that consciousness exists.
